messages.subject: SciCom version 0.4.0
messages.body_plain:
Hello,

I´ve just published version 0.4.0 of SciCom.  SciCom is a Ruby library that allows communication between Ruby and R (using Renjin) in a very transparent way.

I´ve also written a blog post: A (not so) short introduction to SciCom (https://github.com/rbotafogo/scicom/wiki/A-(not-so)-Short-Introduction-to-SciCom) that follows the same examples as A (not so) short introduction to S4 (https://cran.r-project.org/doc/contrib/Genolini-S4tutorialV0-5en.pdf).

I would love to hear feedback about this post and any suggestions, be it about the language, the structure of the post or about the features of SciCom.

Thanks a lot....

--
Rodrigo Botafogo

messages.subject: Renjin Build Robustness
messages.body_plain:
Hi all,

Thanks to some feedback from folks building Renjin from source on Mac OS X, we've done some work to improve the robustness of Renjin's build.

Most importantly, we realized that due to the way Renjin serializes package environments [1], Renjin can *only* be built on case *sensitive* file systems. Mac OS X, for example, may not be case sensitive, though it's pretty straightforward to setup a partition that *is* case sensitive.

Updated build instructions are here:
https://github.com/bedatadriven/renjin/blob/master/BUILDING.md

If you attempt to build on a case-insensitive file system, at least now you will get a nice error message letting you know what the problem instead of apparently random test failures.

Note that this also affects building Renjin using Vagrant, as the Vagrantfile in the Renjin repo creates a shared folder so that Renjin can live on your host file system where you can comfortably work with the source in your IDE of choice.

If you are running windows, I'm afraid right now your only option is to create a VirtualBox image running Linux and checkout the source there within the VM.

Would be very interested to hear if this helps, or anyone else out there has encountered random problems building Renjin from source. If you have an exotic build environment that's important to you, we can set up a Jenkins job to make sure we don't break it for you, as long as you can provide a virtual box image to reproduce your environment.

Thanks!

Alex

[1] See Issue #148 <https://github.com/bedatadriven/renjin/issues/148> for the gorey details.

--
Alex Bertram
Technical Director
bedatadriven

messages.subject: Re: RandomForest in Renjin
messages.body_plain:
A couple people have asked about this package, so here's a quick update:

Basically, we still need to implement a *good* solution for GNU R API methods that involve random number generation and other things that have side effects.

(I have a version of Renjin in the wip-cxx branch that implements a mediocre solution for this problem based on ThreadLocals. You're welcome to build Renjin from this source, and then the randomForest package, but packages built from this branch may *not* work with future releases of Renjin)

Basically, I need to finish a part of GCC-Bridge that transforms native package code to accept an additional parameter with the session context so that multiple Renjin sessions can live in the same process and still share data. I expect that I'll have time to work on that in the coming weeks. But in the meantime, you can see what I've started, and if anyone wants to dig, that would be great!

https://github.com/bedatadriven/renjin/blob/wip-cxx/tools/gnur-compiler/src/main/java/org/renjin/gnur/xform/GlobalVariableEncapsulator.java

Best,
Alex
